subject.title: [Feature]: Skill author-defined setup hook (run skill-supplied script on install/update)

question: Should OpenClaw run skill-authored setup scripts automatically during install/update, keep setup as an explicit admin plugin/RPC action, or first settle the installed-skill Plugin SDK helper surface for external setup plugins?
rationale: Running skill-supplied scripts with selected env values changes the host execution and credential trust boundary, and automation cannot choose the consent, path, env, timeout, logging, ordering, and failure semantics safely.

options.title: Design core lifecycle hook first
options.body: Approve a core install/update setup hook only after maintainers define the prompt/consent, script path containment, env sanitizer, timeout, logging/redaction, and failure semantics.

options.title: Keep explicit plugin RPC
options.body: Treat the ClawHub plugin as the supported manual admin setup path and narrow or reject automatic install/update execution.

options.title: SDK-first external path
options.body: Prioritize the installed-skill SDK helper issue so external setup plugins can share OpenClaw parsing, path, config, and env behavior before any lifecycle hook lands.

recommendation.title: Design core lifecycle hook first
recommendation.body: Approve a core install/update setup hook only after maintainers define the prompt/consent, script path containment, env sanitizer, timeout, logging/redaction, and failure semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses skill install metadata, ClawHub install flows, and install security-gate behavior where steipete has the strongest relevant history.
